info.name: GlobeTrotter — Frontend Routes
info.description:
Postman collection for testing the GlobeTrotter frontend (website/) — every React route and page, the exact API calls each page makes, the UI behavior users see, and the checks to run against each screen.

────────────────────────────────────────────
HOW TO USE
────────────────────────────────────────────
• Local testing:  cd website && npm run dev   → http://localhost:5173 (variable {{webUrl}})
• Deployed testing: set {{webUrl}} to your Netlify/production URL.

• Screen Checks = manual/visual checklist for each page (open {{webUrl}} + path, click through).
• API Behind Screen = the exact request the page fires (identical to the server collection, same {{baseUrl}} + {{accessToken}}), so you can verify the data contract behind the UI.
• Page E2E Flow = full user journeys across screens.

Auth note: the site stores the JWT in localStorage as `token` (plus `user`). On a 401 the axios interceptor clears storage and redirects to /login.

item.description: Pages visible without an account. Inside the app these are wrapped in PublicRoute — if a token exists in localStorage they auto-redirect to /dashboard.

request.description: Manual/visual checks for the itinerary builder screen.
ItineraryPage → POST /trips/:id/stops.

ItineraryPage drag-and-drop → PUT /trips/:id/stops/reorder with { orderedIds }. NOTE: the current backend expects PATCH with { stopIds } — if this returns 404/400 the UI and API have drifted; that is exactly what this check exists to catch.
ItineraryPage → POST /trips/:id/days.

item.name: API Behind Screen — Delete stop activity

request.description: ItineraryPage delete action → DELETE /trips/:id/stops/:stopId/activities/:actId. NOTE: the backend route is actually DELETE /api/trip-activities/:id — this request mirrors what the UI sends today; a 404 here flags a real UI↔API mismatch to fix.

request.description: CreateTripPage → new trip (PUBLIC so it can be shared to the community later).
